subject: science
domain: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer
skillName: We Can See Only When There Is Light

items.prompt:
To see an object, you need
A) light
B) sound
C) wind
D) darkness

steps: You need light shining on the object.

items.prompt:
In a completely dark room, you
A) can see everything
B) cannot see objects
C) see only red
D) see better

steps: With no light, you cannot see.

items.prompt:
To illuminate something means to
A) shine light on it
B) make it dark
C) make it loud
D) hide it

steps: Illuminate means to light something up.

items.prompt:
A book is in a dark closet. When the light goes out, the book
A) disappears
B) is still there, but you cannot see it
C) turns into light
D) makes a sound
items.answer: B) is still there, but you cannot see it

steps: The book is there; you need light to see it.

items.prompt:
A flashlight shines on a chair in a dark room. Now you can see the chair because
A) the chair glows on its own
B) the light illuminates it
C) the chair makes sound
D) it got bigger

steps: The light lets you see the chair.

items.prompt:
To see in a dark room, you should
A) turn on a light or let light in
B) close all windows
C) make noise
D) wait, it will not help
items.answer: A) turn on a light or let light in

steps: Adding light lets you see the objects.

items.prompt:
A shiny toy in a pitch-black room
A) glows on its own so you can see it
B) cannot be seen without light
C) makes its own light
D) disappears forever
items.answer: B) cannot be seen without light

steps: Even a shiny toy needs light to be seen.

items.prompt:
The BEST account of seeing is that objects can be seen
A) only when there is light on them
B) in total darkness
C) only if they are shiny
D) only if they make sound
items.answer: A) only when there is light on them

steps: Light is required to see objects.
